newsitem.title: USA: Marvel bonds up on new reorganization plan.
newsitem.headline: Marvel bonds up on new reorganization plan.

text.p: Bonds of the major creditors for Marvel Entertainment Group Inc traded higher on Monday after news that Ronald Perelman's Andrews Group had withdrawn its reorganization plan, paving the way for passage of an alternative plan by bondholders, dealers said.
"Marvel Holdings 'old' bonds were 22 bid, up 1-3/4 points from Friday's close," said one trader.
Players said all bonds associated with Marvel were better bid, but Marvel Holdings' "old" bonds, which are the most liquid, were the focus of the day.

Bondholders, led by investor Carl Icahn, said Friday that Marvel, which filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in December, agreed to consider their plan to reorganize the company. As a result, Perelman's group withdrew its competing reorganization plan for Marvel.
The bondholders' plan would raise at least $365 million through a pro-rata rights offering that will be guaranteed by Carl Icahn.
Marvel Entertainment Group Inc publishes comic books such as Spider Man and the X-Men. Its three holding companies are Marvel Holdings, Marvel (Parent) Holdings, and Marvel III Holdings.
